Report Series No. 38 B, published by FAO/WHO, Rome 1956.

2.2 SoIublHty
2.2.1 Material is soluble in vegetable oils and chloroform. 2.2.2 Material is insoluble in water and ethanol.

23.4: A solution of the material in chloroform shall turn blue when excess of antimony trichloride ( Carr-Prjce ) reagent ia added.

DJlTllRMJNATION OF PURITY
A-i.. The method as given in Appendix A of IS: 6386-1971t shall be adopted with the following modifications:

a) Measure spectrophotcmerrically the extinction at the absorption maximum (about 449 run) comparing it with the solvent (cyc1ohexane) and utilizing cuvettes of 1 em path-length. Calculate the content using E( 1%. 1 em) <= 2550 for puce ethyl ester of beta-apo-B'ccarctenoic acid.
b) In M ,thod fOT Wat'T-Disp.rsihle Materials - Measure the extinction at the absorption maximum (about 4409 nm) with cyclobeaane as reference solvent and utilizing cuvettes of 1 em path-length. Calculate the content of ethyl ester of beta-apo-St-carotenoic acid, using E( 1%. 1 em) = 2 320. This theoretical value corresponds to the proportion of isomers normally present in these water-dispersible products.
